choices.title: Lithium
choices.correct_explanation:
·       Mood stabilizers are the primary class of medications used to treat bipolar disorder. They work to help stabilize mood and prevent episodes of mania or depression.

·       In this case, the patient has a family history of bipolar disorder and has already experienced three episodes of mania. Lithium is considered the most effective mood stabilizer for treating bipolar disorder, particularly for preventing future episodes of mania.

Incorrect Options:   

·       Option A. Valproate: Valproate is a mood stabilizer that can be used to treat bipolar disorder. However, it is typically more effective at preventing future episodes of depression than mania.     

·       Option B. Lamotrigine: Lamotrigine is a mood stabilizer that can be used to treat bipolar disorder. However, it is less effective at preventing manic episodes than lithium.  

·       Option C. Olanzapine: Olanzapine is an atypical antipsychotic medication that can be used to treat bipolar disorder. It is effective in treating manic episodes but is not typically used as a first-line treatment for bipolar disorder.

choices.correct_explanation:
• In shock, distal pulse is preferred to apical pulse.
  • Shock is defined as a condition in which widespread perfusion to the cells is inadequate to deliver oxygen and nutrients to support vital organs and cellular function. So, the large amount of blood is diverted toward the vital organs as heart, brain and kidney. So, in order to assess the severity of shock, it is essential to assess the distal pulse rather than apical pulse.
  • Arrhythmia is a condition characterized by abnormal rate and rhythm noted in the ECG of the patient. Arrhythmia leads to ineffective cardiac output and altered hemostasis. For example, Sinus tachycardia, sinus bradycardia, Sinus arrhythmia, Supraventricular tachycardia, etc.
  • Hypertension is a silent killer and is defined as BP < 140/90 mmHg. Sequential BP readings are required to diagnose the condition.
  • Heart block is a condition characterized by abnormality in conduction of impulses from SA node to the AV node. There are three degrees of heart blocks.
